content: 1. Doyle et al. (2010) investigated the long-term biological and behavioral effects of an adolescent sexual health intervention in Tanzania through a follow-up survey of the MEMA kwa Vijana Trial. Their findings were published in PLoS Medicine. 2. Ross et al. (2007) conducted a community-randomized trial in Tanzania to assess the biological and behavioral impacts of an adolescent sexual health intervention. The results were detailed in AIDS. 3. Harper et al. (2005) examined the effects of increased access to emergency contraception among young adolescents, with their findings published in Obstetrics & Gynecology. 4. Franklin et al. (2006) conducted a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the effectiveness of Sweet Talk, a text-messaging system designed to support young individuals with diabetes. The study was published in Diabetic Medicine. 5. Chernick et al. (2015) explored methods to enhance the referral of sexually active adolescent females from emergency departments to family planning services. Their findings were published in Journal of Women’s Health. 6. Elliott et al. (2013) questioned whether untargeted sexual health promotion for young people had reached its limit through a quasi-experimental study, with results published in Journal of Epidemiology and Community Health. 7. Funck-Brentano et al. (2005) evaluated the effectiveness of peer support group therapy for HIV-infected adolescents, with their findings published in AIDS. 8. Gilmer et al. (2012) analyzed changes in mental health service utilization when offering youth-specific versus adult programs for transition-age youth. Their study was published in Psychiatric Services. 9. Ngo et al. (2013) assessed the integration of HIV and sexual and reproductive health services for young people in Vietnam through peer-based education. The findings were published in PLoS One. 10. Olson et al. (2008) described the Healthy Teens Counseling Approach, which aimed to change adolescent health behaviors. Their work was published in American Journal of Preventive Medicine. 11. Teasdale et al. (2016) evaluated the impact of youth-friendly services on the retention of 10–24-year-olds in HIV care and treatment programs in Kenya. The study was published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 12. Davila et al. (2013) demonstrated that centralizing HIV services for African-American and Hispanic youth improved retention in care. Their findings were published in AIDS Care. 13. Deogan et al. (2012) estimated the resource needs for adolescent-friendly health services in 74 lowand middle-income countries, with results published in PLoS One. 14. Kempers et al. (2014) conducted a cost analysis and exploratory cost-effectiveness study of youth-friendly sexual and reproductive health services in Moldova, published in BMC Health Services Research. 15. Mark et al. (2017) performed a situational analysis of HIV treatment and care services for adolescents across 23 sub-Saharan African countries, with findings published in Journal of the International AIDS Society. 16. Mellins and Malee (2013) reviewed the mental health challenges faced by youth living with perinatal HIV infection, with their insights published in Journal of the International AIDS Society. 17. Cluver et al. (2019) conducted a prospective cohort study to assess progress toward the UN Sustainable Development Goals for adolescents living with HIV, with results published in The Lancet Child & Adolescent Health. 18. Laurenzi et al. (2020) highlighted the urgent need for evidence on preventing mental health conditions in adolescents living with HIV, as published in Journal of the International AIDS Society. 19. Naar-King et al. (2006) evaluated motivational enhancement therapy for reducing health risk behaviors in HIV-positive youth, with findings published in AIDS Education and Prevention. 20. Rongkavilit et al. (2014) assessed the use of motivational interviewing to address risky sexual behaviors in HIV-positive young Thai men who have sex with men, with results published in Archives of Sexual Behavior. 21. Chen et al. (2011) demonstrated that a clinic-based motivational intervention improved condom use among subgroups of youth living with HIV, as published in Journal of Adolescent Health. 22. Bhana et al. (2014) piloted the VUKA family program, a psychosocial intervention to promote health and mental well-being among HIV-infected early adolescents in South Africa, with findings published in AIDS Care. 23. Bouris et al. (2017) reported on Project nGage, a dyadic network support intervention to retain young Black men who have sex with men in HIV care, with results published in AIDS Behavior. 24. Willis et al. (2019) evaluated the effectiveness of community adolescent treatment supporters (CATS) in improving linkage to care, ART adherence, and psychosocial well-being among adolescents living with HIV in Zimbabwe, with findings published in BMC Public Health. 25. Bermudez et al. (2018) investigated whether economic strengthening interventions improved viral suppression among adolescents living with HIV in Uganda, with results published in AIDS Behavior. 26. Brown et al. (2016) conducted a controlled trial to evaluate the treatment of depressive disorders in adolescents and young adults living with HIV, with findings published in Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes. 27. Denison et al. (2020) assessed the impact of a clinic-based peer mentoring program on viral suppression, adherence, and stigma among HIV-positive youth in Zambia, with results published in PLoS One. 28. Han et al. (2018) conducted a systematic review on eHealth literacy among people living with HIV, with findings published in JMIR Public Health Surveillance. 29. Fatti et al. (2018) evaluated the cost-effectiveness of community-based support for adolescents receiving ART in South Africa, with results published in Journal of the International AIDS Society. 30. Christodoulou et al. (2019) explored the use of active visualization to understand medication adherence among youth living with HIV, with findings published in AIDS Behavior. 31. Spratt et al. (2017) reviewed the use of technology to improve adherence to HIV medications among transitional-age youth, with findings published in Journal of General Medicine. 32. Garofalo et al. (2016) conducted a randomized controlled trial of personalized text message reminders to promote medication adherence among HIV-positive adolescents, with results published in AIDS Behavior. 33. Dulli et al. (2020) evaluated a social media-based support group for youth living with HIV in Nigeria, with findings published in Journal of Medical Internet Research. 34. Mavhu et al. (2020) assessed the impact of a differentiated service delivery model on virological failure in adolescents with HIV in Zimbabwe, with findings published in The Lancet Global Health. 35. Mark et al. (2017) analyzed data from 324 facilities in 30 countries to optimize HIV service delivery for infants, children, and adolescents, with findings published in Journal of the International AIDS Society.
